Issued at 250 AM EST Mon Nov 16 2026

In the near term, patchy fog concerns will be the primary forecast 
issue to deal with. Visibilities early this morning are showing a 
wide range across the region, with lowest vsbys in spots that had a 
more delayed scattering of low cloud cover yesterday afternoon where 
crossover temps were a bit higher. Near term forecast soundings do 
depict some favorable vertical moisture lapse rates for at least 
shallow fog formation this morning and will continue this mention 
through 14Z. Some sporadic one quarter mile visibilities have been 
noted this morning, but especially in favored locations susceptible 
to fog and these lower vsbys. Will continue to monitor trends 
this morning to determine if a more focused Dense Fog Advisory 
will be needed. 

The longwave pattern will finally begin to show some progression 
beginning later today, but this will be a slow process through 
Wednesday as longwave pattern will likely show some resilience 
to change this week with preference to a central CONUS
background longwave ridge. Some low clouds linger across far 
northwest Ohio this morning, but these should begin to diminish 
or shift eastward today as low level winds become more westerly.
Skies should be mostly sunny today with a potential of some low
coverage low clouds mid-late morning with mixing out of shallow
moisture/fog early this morning. Otherwise, a weak mid level 
short wave trough topping the central CONUS ridge into the 
Great Lakes may be enough combined with weak mid level warm 
advection for some patchy high clouds across the southern Great 
Lakes late this afternoon into this evening. With moderation of 
low level airmass and onset of weak low level warm advection 
today, highs in the lower 50s still appear reasonable.

Some better progression in upper pattern is noted late Tuesday 
into Wednesday as an upper level trough approaching the west 
coast today ejects into the northern Plains Wednesday night and 
into southeast Ontario Thursday night. Moisture transport in 
advance of this disturbance still looks to largely 
circumnavigate the local area into Wednesday night as persistent
Mid Atlantic low level anticyclone cuts off Gulf moisture 
transport. Axis of some pre-frontal moisture pooling will 
become weak and elongated in west-east sense across the southern
Great Lakes late Wednesday night into Thursday as the upper 
level short wave has some difficulty in lowering heights with 
much southward extent due to stable nature of wave pattern and 
stubborn breakdown of longwave ridge. PoPs below mentionable 
levels still look appropriate for Thursday/Thursday night with 
perhaps a few sprinkles across western Great Lakes late 
Thursday coincident with the weak elevated moisture axis and
along southern fringe of better short wave trough forcing. A 
transition back to much above normal temperatures is in store 
for Thursday and Friday as expansive homogeneous "warm sector" 
overspreads Ohio Valley and southern Great Lakes.

Induced upper level short wave ridging will build in behind the 
departing northern Great Lakes wave for Friday, while a larger 
scale upper trough digs shifts across the northern Rockies on 
Friday. Overall pattern we have witnessed recently and progged 
to continue in medium range guidance is for lack of 
consolidation/phasing of several negative upper height 
perturbations and a very disjointed nature to wave pattern. As 
a result, stronger upstream frontal convergence with this short 
wave for Saturday looks to wane somewhat with eastward extent as
the trough approaches the western Great Lakes. The transition 
to more progression with these short wave by end of work week 
leaves duration of better low level moisture transport more 
limited with northward extent with better moisture quality 
confined to the central/southern Plains. Nonetheless, would 
expect a somewhat more impressive narrow pooled moisture axis to
work into the area Saturday and Saturday night with better 
chance of some isoalted-scattered frontally induced showers. 
Highs will remain well above normal Saturday in advance of this
wave cooling back to the mid 50s for second half of the 
weekend.

The frontal boundary from weekend system will probably hang up 
across the local area to begin next week as medium range guidance 
depicts a generally low amplitude flow setup. This should
support temps at or slightly below normal to begin the week. 
Possibility of lingering baroclinic zone across the region and 
additional eastern Pacific waves in this more suppressed low 
amplitude pattern could be favorable for additional short 
waves/weak to modest advective forcing episodes that would 
support some precip chances next week. However, this appears 
more likely beyond this forecast valid period and is of very low
confidence at this time.
